matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy that must be resolved.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick equation, to know what change is needed.
matchstick.example: Skipping the initial calculation and moving a stick arbitrarily, resulting in an equation that still doesn't balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all possible source characters (numerals or operators) and all possible target characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the needed numeric change, generate all candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Considering only moves that change a numeral but overlooking moves that affect operators, missing the correct solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the move changes the numeric values of the affected numerals and operators, and keep only moves that exactly offset the initial discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating candidate transformations, to filter out those that don't fix the equation.
matchstick.example: Choosing a stick move that changes the left side by +1 while the right side changes by +2, leaving the equation unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character, changing its orientation or position to transform the character into another valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If no inter‑character move yields a solution, explore reshaping a single character.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of reshaping a V into an X by repositioning its sticks, thus missing a valid transformation.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a '-' sign, and moving a stick onto a '-' can turn it back into '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment can be achieved by changing the equality sign into a subtraction sign (or vice versa).
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn '=' into a '+' by adding a vertical stick, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick converts it into '-', and adding a vertical stick to '-' creates '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution may involve converting between addition and subtraction operators.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal stick from '+' and leaving a lone vertical stick, which is not a recognized operator.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, ensure both source and target remain valid Roman numerals or operators after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For any candidate transformation that transfers a stick between different characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from X to V, leaving X as a single diagonal (invalid).

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., turning '=' into '-' and '-' into '=').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both source and target are operators and swapping a stick can adjust the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-', but forgetting to adjust the '-' to become '=', resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, ensure that the source character can lose that stick and still represent a valid numeral, or be removed entirely if it becomes empty.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, to avoid leaving an invalid fragment.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from V, leaving a single diagonal line that does not correspond to any Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.title: Allow removal of a single‑stick numeral
matchstick.principle: If a numeral consists of a single stick (e.g., I), moving that stick is allowed and the numeral can disappear; the equation remains valid as long as the remaining characters form a proper expression.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the only stick in a numeral is the source of a relocation.
matchstick.example: Rejecting a move that takes the only stick from an I, causing the I to vanish, even though the resulting equation is syntactically correct.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a character without checking whether the remaining sticks still form a valid Roman numeral or operator, resulting in an impossible shape.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that the source character, after losing the stick, corresponds to a known valid character (or disappears if it was a single‑stick numeral).

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation but does not recompute the numeric values of both sides, so the final equation may still be false.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the integer values of the left and right sides after applying a move and confirm they are equal before outputting the answer.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may inadvertently delete a character or forget to include an operator, producing an incomplete expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the full sequence of characters; if a character loses its only stick, it may be removed, but ensure the overall syntax (including operators and equality) remains intact.

matchstick.description: Attempting to change '=' into an invalid operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tries to repurpose the '=' sign by moving a stick in a way that yields a shape not recognized as a valid operator (e.g., a diagonal line).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only transform '=' into '-' (by removing one horizontal) or into '+' (by adding a vertical); never into shapes that are not defined operators.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes an operator (e.g., from '-' to '+') without accounting for how that changes the arithmetic on the right side, leading to a mismatched equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is altered, recalculate the expression using the new operator and ensure the resulting numeric values still satisfy the equality.
